items.title: Preston Jackson Interview, 1973-09-07
items.q: I also attended school with Earl Humphrey. I lived just a few blocks from Humphrey at one time.

ctx.x: Well, as you grew on in years, did you hear any more music?

Oh yeah, I, in spite of me hearing this music, I used to say, the second line just like the rest of the kids. We used to try sometime way away from home, you know, out of the neighborhood. I remember I, I think it was about the 30th of May and some friends of mine and I, we, we came all the way down to French Bar Town and the boys got behind us and ran us all the way to the podgers and ramparts, you know. And so I always did love music. I used to do a lot of whistling. I still do. And so, but I didn't have no…
Where was he from? He's from New Orleans.

items.title: Preston Jackson Interview, 1958-06-02
items.q: His brother Earl was a trombone player

ctx.x: See what I'm talking about? So I mean I lived right across the street from Professor George Correa, and when I lived on Upper Line Street I was only two blocks from the Humphreys, and Mrs. Humphrey, old man Humphrey's daughter, taught me in the fourth grade at Tarly Farm School. And she taught us a little music there. And so she knew music and evidently I think she must have gotten from her father. And Willie Humphrey today, if he's still living, he reads a lot of music. His brother Earl was a trombone player,…
Well he's in the Eureka, the trumpet player, and he's the leader of the Eureka band, the brass band.
